title: Aurum Alpha secret declaration
description: standards/032-secrets.md SE2: the declaration a service carries beside its deployables, listing every secret its processes read. It is the secret half of the configuration declaration 030 SC3 anticipates: a process reads exactly the variables it declares, and the ones marked here are the ones the platform delivers as secrets, the log emitter redacts by value (SE5), the image set carries by the least-credential rule (SE6), and the rotation check ages (SE7). A secret in a process's environment that is not declared here is a finding; a secret declared here and absent at start blocks serving (SC3) or exits 78 (035 WK4). schema_version 1 - evolves additively per PC6.

secretName.description: SE3 grammar: <SUBJECT>_<KIND>. SUBJECT is the backing service's logical name in SCREAMING_SNAKE_CASE (DATABASE, SMTP, STRIPE, SESSION), KIND is one of the closed set (PASSWORD, SECRET, TOKEN, API_KEY, URL, DSN, SIGNING_KEY, ENCRYPTION_KEY, PRIVATE_KEY_FILE). A bare kind (PASSWORD) has no subject and is refused; an environment name as the leading segment (PROD_, STAGING_) is refused because per factor III a deployment differs by value, never by which variable is read.

image.description: The image roles of 010 Principle 15 and 035 WK2: the request-serving server, the pool worker, the one-shot jobs image, the migrate image.

secret.description: One declared secret. The conditional rules below are the ones prose states and a reviewer would otherwise have to remember: the name's kind suffix agrees with kind; a private key is a file; a file-delivered secret carries an absolute path and a _FILE name; a static secret carries a maximum age; the migrate image shares no secret with any other image (025 SD3, 035 WK8).

id.description: SE2/SE8. The secret's own public id, minted once when it is declared and never reused. It is what an audit event names as its target when the secret is rotated or revoked (080 AE2 requires a public id), so the record survives a rename of the variable.

name.description: SE3. The environment variable the process reads. For delivery: file it is the variable holding the path, and the file's content is the secret.

kind.description: SE2. What the material is, which decides its name suffix, its delivery and its redaction: a connection_string registers its userinfo password as a redacted value as well as the whole string (SE5).

delivery.description: SE1. env: the value is the variable's value. file: the variable's value is an absolute path the platform mounts the material at before the process starts; used for material too large or too sensitive for an environment string - a private key, a multi-line PEM.

path.description: SE1. Required when delivery is file: the absolute path the platform mounts the material at, identical in every environment so the image is environment-agnostic.

purpose.description: SE2. What the process does with it, in one sentence, so a reviewer can ask whether the image that carries it needs it.

backing_service.description: SE2/SE6. The logical name of the backing service the secret grants access to (factor IV), identical across environments; 'self' for material the service alone holds, such as its own session signing key. One credential per backing service per service is checked over this field.

owner.description: SE7. The team or role that rotates it and answers for it. A secret with no owner is a secret nobody rotates.

issued_by.description: SE6. platform: short-lived, issued to the workload by the platform (workload identity, an IAM role, OIDC federation) and re-issued without anyone acting. static: a long-lived value someone created and someone must rotate - the fallback where the backing service offers nothing better.

max_age_days.description: SE7. Required for a static secret: the longest it may go unrotated. Default ninety days; the ceiling is one year, because a credential older than that has outlived every person who knew where it was used. A static secret whose last rotation is older than this is a finding.

rotation.description: SE7. How this secret is rotated without a code change.

mode.description: restart: the new value is delivered and the processes are restarted, because a process reads its secrets at start (SE1). dual_window: the backing service honours two valid credentials at once, so the new one is issued, delivered, the processes restarted, and the old one revoked after - the only static mode with no unverifiable moment. reissue: platform-issued only; the platform renews the material in place before it expires and the process re-reads the file on each use.

procedure.description: The repository-relative path of the operations document that states the procedure, which is where AGENTS.md rule 3 puts every procedure a human runs.

images.description: SE6. Which of the service's images carry this secret. The least its jobs declare (035 WK8); the migrate image carries the migration credential and nothing else (025 SD3).

allOf.description: SE3: the name's kind suffix says what the material is, so the suffix and the kind agree.
SE1: a file-delivered secret names its path and its variable ends in _FILE; an environment-delivered one has no path and does not.
SE1: a private key is never an environment string.

SE7: a static secret declares how old it may get and is rotated by restart or dual window. A platform-issued one is re-issued on the platform's schedule, may omit the age, and its rotation mode is reissue.
SE6, 025 SD3, 035 WK8: a secret the migrate image carries is carried by no other image.

service.description: The service's stable name, identical to the log line's service field (030 SC2) and the provenance block's (SC5).

secrets.description: SE2. Every secret any process of this service reads. Empty is a valid declaration and a strong claim.
